claims.text: WTaTiVZr is an equimolar alloy containing 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
WTaTiVZr has a refined multiphase microstructure.
WTaTiVZr contains nanoscale precipitates and heterogeneous grain boundaries.
Commercially used pure tungsten has a relatively homogeneous microstructure and lacks the heterogeneity attributed to WTaTiVZr.
The refined multiphase microstructure is the primary cause of greater plastic strain and toughness in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
Precipitates in refractory high-entropy alloys can produce dispersion strengthening.
Nanoscale precipitates and heterogeneous grain boundaries in WTaTiVZr act as crack-deflection sites.
The same microstructural features facilitate easier dislocation movement in WTaTiVZr.
Microstructural heterogeneity lowers local stress concentrations in WTaTiVZr.
Crack deflection and increased dislocation mobility enhance plastic deformation and toughness.
WTaTiVZr has a reduced brittle-to-ductile transition relative to pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature tests, WTaTiVZr will have significantly greater plastic strain to failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature tests, WTaTiVZr will have significantly greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Post-test microscopy will show crack deflection or bridging associated with precipitates and grain-boundary heterogeneity in WTaTiVZr.
Pure tungsten will exhibit more limited dislocation movement and greater stress concentration than WTaTiVZr.
The proposed mechanism remains valid while the multiphase microstructure is stable, approximately up to 1100–1300 degrees Celsius.
At higher temperatures, precipitate coarsening or phase transformations will diminish the mechanical benefits of the refined microstructure.
Tests at or above 1000 degrees Celsius simulate high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
Prior studies on related refractory high-entropy alloys support a correlation between multiphase or dispersion-strengthened structures and improved mechanical performance.
Identically processed WTaTiVZr and pure-tungsten specimens tested under the same conditions provide a controlled comparison.

contradictions.description: The precipitates are described both as obstacles to dislocation motion and as features that facilitate easier dislocation movement, without explaining how these opposing effects coexist.
